name: Antipsychotic Long-Acting

fields.mechanism_of_action: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: this monograph covers the depot/long-acting injectable antipsychotic class, not a single molecule. Each depot product is the long-acting ester or salt of an antipsychotic and has the same central mechanism as its oral parent, differing only in release kinetics. Haloperidol decanoate: the mechanism of action of haloperidol for the treatment of schizophrenia is unclear, but its efficacy could be mediated through its activity as an antagonist at central dopamine type 2 receptors; haloperidol also binds to alpha-1 adrenergic receptors with lower affinity and displays minimal binding to muscarinic cholinergic and histaminergic (H1) receptors (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY). Fluphenazine decanoate: the mechanism whereby its therapeutic action is exerted is unknown; fluphenazine has activity at all levels of the central nervous system, is more potent on a milligram basis, less potentiating of CNS depressants and anaesthetics, less sedating and less likely than some older phenothiazines to produce hypotension than some phenothiazines (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY). Risperidone: the mechanism of action of risperidone in schizophrenia is unclear, and its therapeutic activity could be mediated through a combination of dopamine Type 2 (D2) and serotonin Type 2 (5-HT2) receptor antagonism; the clinical effect results from the combined concentrations of risperidone and its major active metabolite 9-hydroxyrisperidone (paliperidone) (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 12.1). Paliperidone: the mechanism of action of paliperidone is unclear, but its therapeutic effect in schizophrenia could be mediated through a combination of central dopamine D2 and serotonin 5-HT2A receptor antagonism (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 12.1). Olanzapine: the mechanism of action of olanzapine in the listed indications is unclear, but its efficacy in schizophrenia could be mediated through a combination of dopamine and serotonin type 2 (5-HT2) antagonism (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 12.1).
indications: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: indications differ by product and are listed per product below. Haloperidol decanoate: treatment of patients with schizophrenia who require prolonged parenteral antipsychotic therapy (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, INDICATIONS AND USAGE).

Fluphenazine decanoate: a long-acting parenteral antipsychotic drug intended for use in the management of patients requiring prolonged parenteral neuroleptic therapy (e.g. chronic schizophrenics); it has not been shown effective in the management of behavioral complications in patients with mental retardation (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, INDICATIONS AND USAGE).

RISPERDAL CONSTA (risperidone): treatment of schizophrenia; and as monotherapy or as adjunctive therapy to lithium or valproate for the maintenance treatment of Bipolar I Disorder (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 1).

UZEDY (risperidone, subcutaneous extended release): treatment of schizophrenia in adults; and as monotherapy or as adjunctive therapy to lithium or valproate for the maintenance treatment of bipolar I disorder in adults (UZEDY label, section 1).

INVEGA SUSTENNA (paliperidone palmitate, once monthly): treatment of schizophrenia in adults; and schizoaffective disorder in adults as monotherapy and as an adjunct to mood stabilizers or antidepressants (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 1).

INVEGA TRINZA (paliperidone palmitate, every three months): treatment of schizophrenia in patients after they have been adequately treated with INVEGA SUSTENNA for at least four months (INVEGA TRINZA label, section 1).

INVEGA HAFYERA (paliperidone palmitate, every six months): treatment of schizophrenia in adults after they have been adequately treated with either a once-a-month paliperidone palmitate extended-release injectable suspension for at least four months, or an every-three-month paliperidone palmitate extended-release injectable suspension for at least one three-month injection cycle (INVEGA HAFYERA label, section 1).
ZYPREXA RELPREVV (olanzapine pamoate): treatment of schizophrenia; efficacy was established in two clinical trials in adults (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 1.1).

WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (24th list, 2025): fluphenazine, parenteral general injections IM 25 mg per mL in ampoule (decanoate) and 25 mg per mL in ampoule (enanthate), section 'Medicines for psychotic disorders', indication 'Schizophrenia or other primary psychotic disorders'; haloperidol decanoate, section 'Medicines for psychotic disorders', therapeutic equivalent to fluphenazine for schizophrenia or other primary psychotic disorders (WHO eEML, entries 273 and 305)

Kenya Essential Medicines List 2023: fluphenazine injection (oily, depot) 25 mg (as decanoate)/1 mL ampoule, Level of Use 4 (primary hospital); haloperidol injection (oily) 50 mg/1 mL ampoule, Level of Use 4 (primary hospital) (KEML 2023, entries 25.1.5 and 25.1.6)
contraindications: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: contraindications differ by product. Haloperidol decanoate: severe toxic central nervous system depression or comatose states from any cause; hypersensitivity to haloperidol (anaphylactic reaction and angioedema have been reported); Parkinson's disease; dementia with Lewy bodies (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).

Fluphenazine decanoate: suspected or established subcortical brain damage; patients receiving large doses of hypnotics; comatose or severely depressed states; the presence of blood dyscrasia or liver damage; not intended for use in children under 12 years of age; hypersensitivity to fluphenazine, with cross-sensitivity to phenothiazine derivatives possible (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, CONTRAINDICATIONS).

RISPERDAL CONSTA: known hypersensitivity to risperidone or paliperidone, or to any excipient in the formulation; hypersensitivity reactions including anaphylaxis and angioedema have been reported (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 4).
UZEDY: known hypersensitivity to risperidone, its metabolite paliperidone, or to any of its components (UZEDY label, section 4).

INVEGA SUSTENNA, INVEGA TRINZA and INVEGA HAFYERA: known hypersensitivity to paliperidone or risperidone, or to any excipient in the formulation (INVEGA SUSTENNA section 4; INVEGA TRINZA section 4; INVEGA HAFYERA section 4).
ZYPREXA RELPREVV: none. The label states 'Contraindications: None' (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 4).
side_effects: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: extrapyramidal symptoms are the hallmark of the depot first-generation antipsychotics and were more frequent with fluphenazine decanoate than haloperidol decanoate in a head-to-head double-blind trial (n=36 each): parkinsonism 30.6% (haloperidol decanoate) versus 44.4% (fluphenazine decanoate), akinesia 2.8% versus 22.2%, akathisia 2.8% versus 13.9%, oculogyric crisis 5.6% versus 0%, tremor 2.8% versus 0% (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, ADVERSE REACTIONS, Table 1)

Fluphenazine decanoate: the side effects most frequently reported with phenothiazine compounds are extrapyramidal symptoms including pseudoparkinsonism, dystonia, dyskinesia, akathisia, oculogyric crises, opisthotonos and hyperreflexia; muscle rigidity sometimes accompanied by hyperthermia has been reported; a higher incidence of extrapyramidal reactions is expected with fluphenazine decanoate than with less potent piperazine derivatives or straight-chain phenothiazines such as chlorpromazine (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, ADVERSE REACTIONS and PRECAUTIONS)

INVEGA SUSTENNA: the most common (at least 5% in any group) and likely drug-related adverse reactions in the double-blind, placebo-controlled schizophrenia trials were injection site reactions, somnolence/sedation, dizziness, akathisia and extrapyramidal disorder; adverse reactions occurring more frequently than with placebo by 2% or more were weight increased, nasopharyngitis, headache, hyperprolactinemia and pyrexia (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 6.1)

RISPERDAL CONSTA: somnolence was reported by 5% of patients in multiple-dose trials; syncope 0.8% (12/1499) and seizures 0.3% (5/1499) in premarketing testing; orthostatic hypotension with dizziness, tachycardia and in some patients syncope; hyperprolactinemia (risperidone is associated with higher prolactin elevation than other antipsychotic agents); metabolic changes including hyperglycaemia, dyslipidaemia and weight gain; falls; dysphagia and aspiration pneumonia; priapism; leukopenia/neutropenia/agranulocytosis (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, sections 5.5-5.13 and 6.1)

ZYPREXA RELPREVV: post-injection delirium/sedation syndrome - adverse events with signs and symptoms consistent with olanzapine overdose, in particular sedation (including coma) and/or delirium - occurred in less than 0.1% of injections and in approximately 2% of patients who received injections for up to 46 months; other symptoms included extrapyramidal symptoms, dysarthria, ataxia, aggression, dizziness, weakness, hypertension and convulsion (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 5.1)

Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS): a potentially fatal symptom complex with hyperpyrexia, muscle rigidity, altered mental status and autonomic instability, reported with antipsychotic drugs including haloperidol, fluphenazine, risperidone, paliperidone and olanzapine (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 5.3; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.3; ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 17)

Tardive dyskinesia: a syndrome of potentially irreversible, involuntary, dyskinetic movements may develop with antipsychotic treatment; risk and likelihood of irreversibility increase with duration of treatment and total cumulative dose, and the syndrome can develop after relatively brief treatment at low doses (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.5)

Hyperprolactinemia: D2 antagonism elevates prolactin with persistence during chronic administration, causing galactorrhoea, amenorrhoea, gynaecomastia and impotence; long-standing hyperprolactinemia with hypogonadism may lead to decreased bone density (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.10; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 5.6)

Metabolic changes: hyperglycaemia and diabetes mellitus (in some cases extreme, with ketoacidosis, hyperosmolar coma or death), dyslipidaemia and weight gain are class risks of atypical antipsychotics, with each drug having its own specific risk profile (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.6)

Cardiovascular: QTc interval prolongation and Torsades de Pointes with haloperidol, with a QTc exceeding 500 msec associated with increased risk; paliperidone causes a modest increase in the corrected QT interval (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.4)

Orthostatic hypotension and syncope: paliperidone can induce orthostatic hypotension and syncope through alpha-adrenergic blocking activity, reported in less than 1% (4/1293) of INVEGA SUSTENNA subjects versus 0% (0/510) with placebo (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.7)

Falls: somnolence, postural hypotension and motor and sensory instability reported with antipsychotics including haloperidol decanoate, fluphenazine decanoate, risperidone and paliperidone may lead to falls and consequent fractures or other fall-related injuries (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.8)

Fluphenazine decanoate additional class-consistent effects: hepatic injury with cholestatic jaundice, particularly during the first months of therapy; blood dyscrasias including leukopenia, agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenic and non-thrombocytopenic purpura, eosinophilia and pancytopenia; skin reactions including photosensitivity and exfoliative dermatitis; weight change, peripheral oedema, abnormal lactation, gynaecomastia, menstrual irregularities, impotency and increased libido; 'silent pneumonias'; sudden unexpected and unexplained deaths in hospitalised psychotic patients, with autopsy findings usually revealing acute fulminating pneumonia or pneumonitis, aspiration of gastric contents or intramyocardial lesions (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS and ADVERSE REACTIONS)

Injection-site and local reactions: injection site reaction is reported with haloperidol decanoate; INVEGA TRINZA must be shaken vigorously for at least 15 seconds and injected within 5 minutes to avoid an incomplete administration and needle blockage, and in the event of an incompletely administered dose the remainder must not be re-injected (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, ADVERSE REACTIONS; INVEGA TRINZA label, section 2.1)

dosage.adult: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: there is no single class dose. Each depot product below has its own dosing, interval and route, and the figures for one product must not be applied to another. HALOPERIDOL DECANOATE (100 mg/mL in sesame oil, IM): convert from oral haloperidol using an initial depot dose of 10 to 20 times the previous daily oral haloperidol dose; 10 to 15 times for elderly, debilitated or low-dose (up to 10 mg/day oral) patients; 20 times for patients previously on higher doses at risk of relapse or tolerant to haloperidol, with downward titration on succeeding injections. The initial dose must not exceed 100 mg regardless of previous requirements; if more than 100 mg is required, give it as two injections (maximum 100 mg initially, then the balance in 3 to 7 days). Maintenance is usually 10 to 15 times the previous daily oral dose, individualised by clinical response; it is usually given monthly or every 4 weeks, and clinical experience above 450 mg per month is limited (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION). FLUPHENAZINE DECANOATE (25 mg/mL in sesame oil, IM or SC): initiate with 12.5 to 25 mg (0.5 to 1 mL); onset of action generally appears at 24 to 72 hours and the effect on psychotic symptoms becomes significant within 48 to 96 hours; subsequent injections and the dosing interval are determined by response, and a single injection may control symptoms for up to four weeks or longer, with the response to a single dose found to last as long as six weeks in a few maintenance patients. It is advisable to treat patients with no history of phenothiazine use with a shorter-acting form of fluphenazine first to establish response and appropriate dosage (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION). RISPERDAL CONSTA (IM): 25 mg every 2 weeks for schizophrenia and for maintenance treatment of Bipolar I Disorder; some patients not responding to 25 mg may benefit from 37.5 mg or 50 mg, and the maximum dose should not exceed 50 mg every 2 weeks. A lower initial dose of 12.5 mg may be appropriate with hepatic or renal impairment, with certain drug interactions that increase risperidone plasma concentrations, or with a history of poor tolerability. Oral risperidone (or another antipsychotic) must be given with the first injection and continued for 3 weeks, then discontinued. Upward dose adjustment should not be made more frequently than every 4 weeks (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, sections 2.1-2.3). UZEDY (subcutaneous extended release): switch from oral daily risperidone, initiating UZEDY the day after the last oral dose, with no loading dose and no supplemental oral risperidone - oral 2 mg/day corresponds to 50 mg monthly or 100 mg every 2 months; 3 mg to 75 mg or 150 mg; 4 mg to 100 mg or 200 mg; 5 mg to 125 mg or 250 mg (UZEDY label, sections 2.1-2.2). INVEGA SUSTENNA (once monthly, IM): initiate with 234 mg in the deltoid on day 1 and 156 mg in the deltoid on day 8, then monthly maintenance from week 5; for schizophrenia 39-234 mg monthly (recommended 117 mg, maximum 234 mg) and for schizoaffective disorder 78-234 mg monthly (maximum 234 mg); the 39 mg strength was not studied in the long-term schizoaffective disorder study. Patients never treated with oral paliperidone or oral or injectable risperidone should first establish tolerability with oral paliperidone or oral risperidone (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 2.2). INVEGA TRINZA (every three months): only after adequate INVEGA SUSTENNA for at least four months, with the last two SUSTENNA doses the same strength; 78 mg becomes 273 mg, 117 mg becomes 410 mg, 156 mg becomes 546 mg and 234 mg becomes 819 mg, then every 3 months with adjustment in the 273-819 mg range (INVEGA TRINZA label, section 2.2). INVEGA HAFYERA (every six months, gluteal IM only): initiate only after adequate PP1M treatment for at least four months or one PP3M cycle; from PP1M, 117 mg becomes 1092 mg and 234 mg becomes 1560 mg; from PP3M, 273 mg becomes 819 mg, 410 mg becomes 1092 mg and 546 mg becomes 1560 mg; thereafter every 6 months with adjustment between 1092 mg and 1560 mg (INVEGA HAFYERA label, sections 2.1-2.2). ZYPREXA RELPREVV (olanzapine pamoate, deep IM gluteal only): 150 mg, 210 mg or 300 mg every 2 weeks, or 405 mg every 4 weeks, by healthcare professional, after establishing tolerability with oral olanzapine; dose correspondence to oral olanzapine is 10 mg/day to 210 mg or 150 mg every 2 weeks or 405 mg every 4 weeks, 15 mg/day to 300 mg every 2 weeks, and 20 mg/day to 300 mg every 2 weeks; maintenance after 8 weeks is 300 mg, 210 mg or 405 mg every 4 weeks, or 300 mg every 2 weeks (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 2.1).
dosage.geriatric: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: geriatric handling is product-specific. Haloperidol decanoate: clinical studies did not include sufficient numbers of subjects aged 65 and over; the prevalence of tardive dyskinesia appears highest among the elderly, especially elderly women, and the pharmacokinetics of haloperidol in geriatric patients generally warrant the use of lower doses, so an initial depot dose of 10 to 15 times the previous daily oral dose is appropriate (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION and Geriatric Use). INVEGA SUSTENNA: no specific geriatric dose is specified, but orthostatic hypotension and syncope, falls and cerebrovascular risk are all more consequential in elderly patients (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, sections 5.2, 5.7 and 5.8). RISPERDAL CONSTA: use with particular caution in the elderly and in patients with renal or hepatic impairment (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 5.7).
dosage.paediatric: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: paediatric use is not established for the depot products in this entry. Haloperidol decanoate: safety and effectiveness in children have not been established (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, PEDIATRIC USE). Fluphenazine decanoate: not intended for use in children under 12 years of age; safety and efficacy in children have not been established (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, CONTRAINDICATIONS and PRECAUTIONS). RISPERDAL CONSTA, UZEDY, INVEGA SUSTENNA, INVEGA TRINZA, INVEGA HAFYERA and ZYPREXA RELPREVV are indicated in adults, with ZYPREXA RELPREVV's efficacy established in adult trials (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 1; UZEDY label, section 1; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 1; INVEGA HAFYERA label, section 1; ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 1.1).

interactions: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: the depot products share several interaction mechanisms but the specifics are product-specific. QT prolongation: haloperidol decanoate - use with caution in patients with QT-prolongation conditions and with drugs known to prolong the QTc interval, including class 1A antiarrhythmics (procainamide, quinidine, disopyramide), class 3 antiarrhythmics (amiodarone, sotalol), and drugs such as citalopram, erythromycin, levofloxacin, methadone and ziprasidone; caution is also advised with drugs causing electrolyte imbalance (diuretics, corticosteroids) because hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia and hypocalcaemia are risk factors for QT prolongation (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, DRUG INTERACTIONS). Paliperidone - avoid combination with other QTc-prolonging drugs including class 1A (quinidine, procainamide) and class III (amiodarone, sotalol) antiarrhythmics, antipsychotics (chlorpromazine, thioridazine), antibiotics (gatifloxacin, moxifloxacin), and avoid in congenital long QT syndrome or a history of cardiac arrhythmias (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.4).

CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 inhibition increases haloperidol plasma concentrations and the risk of QTc prolongation - examples of CYP3A4 inhibitors are alprazolam, itraconazole, ketoconazole, nefazodone and ritonavir; CYP2D6 inhibitors are chlorpromazine, promethazine, quinidine, paroxetine, sertraline and venlafaxine; combined inhibitors are fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, ritonavir and buspirone. Patients on these combinations should be monitored for increased or prolonged pharmacologic effects and the haloperidol decanoate dose decreased as necessary (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, DRUG INTERACTIONS).

CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: potent CYP3A4 inducers may reduce antipsychotic exposure and efficacy - with haloperidol decanoate, rifampin lowered plasma haloperidol by a mean of 70% with an increase in Brief Psychiatric Rating Scale scores, and carbamazepine produced a linear fall in haloperidol concentrations with increasing carbamazepine concentrations; during combined treatment the haloperidol decanoate dose should be increased or the interval adjusted, and after withdrawal of the inducer the dose or interval may need reducing (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, DRUG INTERACTIONS). For INVEGA SUSTENNA, avoid using a strong inducer of CYP3A4 and/or P-glycoprotein (e.g. carbamazepine, rifampin, St John's Wort) during the 1-month dosing interval if possible (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 2.5).

CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: central nervous system depressants - haloperidol may potentiate CNS depressants such as anaesthetics, opioids and alcohol, and the use of alcohol with haloperidol decanoate should be avoided due to possible additive effects and hypotension (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, DRUG INTERACTIONS and INFORMATION FOR PATIENTS); phenothiazine derivatives including fluphenazine decanoate can potentiate central nervous system depressants (opiates, analgesics, antihistamines, barbiturates, alcohol) (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS).

CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: lithium - an encephalopathic syndrome characterised by weakness, lethargy, fever, tremulousness and confusion, extrapyramidal symptoms, leukocytosis, elevated serum enzymes, BUN and fasting blood sugar, followed by irreversible brain damage, has occurred in a few patients treated with lithium plus haloperidol; a causal relationship has not been established, but patients on combined therapy should be monitored closely for early neurological toxicity and treatment discontinued promptly if such signs appear (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS).
CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: valproate - sodium valproate, a drug known to inhibit glucuronidation, does not affect haloperidol plasma concentrations (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, DRUG INTERACTIONS).

CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: concomitant risperidone or oral paliperidone with paliperidone palmitate - since paliperidone is the major active metabolite of risperidone, caution should be exercised when INVEGA SUSTENNA is coadministered with risperidone or oral paliperidone for extended periods, and safety data involving concomitant use with other antipsychotics is limited (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 2.4).

CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: antihypertensives - clinically significant hypotension has been observed with concomitant use of oral RISPERDAL and antihypertensive medication (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 5.7).
fields.monitoring: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: monitor the extrapyramidal system (parkinsonism, akathisia, dystonia, tremor) and use a systematic scale such as AIMS for tardive dyskinesia, reducing the dose periodically if clinically possible because antipsychotics can mask the syndrome (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS). Monitor temperature, mental status, autonomic signs, creatine phosphokinase, leukocytosis and renal function for neuroleptic malignant syndrome (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS). Monitor prolactin, with the understanding that hyperprolactinemia may suppress GnRH and impair gonadal function (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.10). Monitor weight, body mass index, fasting blood glucose and lipids for metabolic changes (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.6). Monitor ECG/QTc, electrolytes (particularly potassium and magnesium) and cardiac history, especially with haloperidol decanoate and paliperidone (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.4). Monitor orthostatic vital signs in patients vulnerable to hypotension, and assess fall risk at initiation and recurrently during long-term antipsychotic therapy, particularly in the elderly (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, sections 5.7 and 5.8; Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS). Monitor the complete blood count for leukopenia/neutropenia/agranulocytosis, particularly in the first few months of therapy and after discontinuation; discontinue with severe neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count < 1000/mm3) (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.9). Monitor for hyperglycaemia symptoms (polydipsia, polyuria, polyphagia, weakness) and perform fasting blood glucose testing at the start and periodically (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.6). Monitor hepatic function, renal function and the blood picture during long-term phenothiazine therapy with fluphenazine decanoate; discontinue treatment if BUN becomes abnormal or if cholestatic jaundice develops (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS). For ZYPREXA RELPREVV, monitor each patient in a certified healthcare setting for at least 3 hours after every injection for post-injection delirium/sedation syndrome, and confirm that the patient is alert and oriented before release (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, sections 2.1 and 5.1). For INVEGA HAFYERA, INVEGA TRINZA and INVEGA SUSTENNA, monitor response and tolerability after each dose adjustment, since the full effect may not be evident for several months (INVEGA HAFYERA label, section 2.2).
fields.patient_counselling: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY. Explain that a depot antipsychotic is a long-acting form of an antipsychotic that is given by injection at intervals of weeks to months, that oral tolerability must first be established with the oral form of the same or a related antipsychotic, and that a dose missed is not 'topped up' - the label of the specific product must be followed (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 2.3; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 2.2; ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 2.1; UZEDY label, section 2.1). Warn patients and caregivers about neuroleptic malignant syndrome (high fever, severe muscle stiffness, confusion, fast heart rate, sweating) and about tardive dyskinesia (involuntary movements of the tongue, face, mouth or trunk), instructing them to seek medical review promptly (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 17). Advise patients that antipsychotics may impair the mental and/or physical abilities required for hazardous tasks such as operating machinery or driving a motor vehicle, and that alcohol should be avoided because of possible additive effects and hypotension (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, INFORMATION FOR PATIENTS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.11). Advise patients to report mood swings, agitation, drowsiness, dizziness on standing, tremor, stiffness, akathisia (restlessness), stiffness of the jaw or neck, fever, sore throat or bruising, and any new involuntary movements (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS and PRECAUTIONS; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, sections 5.7 and 5.10). For ZYPREXA RELPREVV, counsel specifically about post-injection delirium/sedation syndrome: the patient must be observed at the healthcare setting for at least 3 hours after every injection, must be accompanied to their destination, should not drive or operate heavy machinery for the remainder of the day of each injection, and should remain vigilant for symptoms and able to obtain medical assistance (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, sections 5.2 and 17). Advise patients that antipsychotics may cause dizziness on standing and falls, and that fall risk should be reported (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.8). For all depot products, remind the patient that the injection must be given by a healthcare professional and that injection site reactions are common (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 6.1).
warnings: CLASS WARNING (boxed, present on all products in this entry except where otherwise noted): increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis. Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs are at an increased risk of death; analyses of seventeen placebo-controlled trials (modal duration 10 weeks), largely in patients taking atypical antipsychotic drugs, revealed a risk of death in drug-treated patients of between 1.6 and 1.7 times the risk in placebo-treated patients, with a rate of death of about 4.5% in drug-treated patients versus about 2.6% with placebo over a typical 10-week controlled trial; most deaths appeared cardiovascular or infectious in nature. None of the depot products in this entry is approved for dementia-related psychosis (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, Boxed Warning; Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, Boxed Warning; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, Boxed Warning; UZEDY label, Boxed Warning; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, Boxed Warning; INVEGA TRINZA label, Boxed Warning; INVEGA HAFYERA label, Boxed Warning; ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, Boxed Warning)

ZYPREXA RELPREVV boxed warning (additional, product-specific): post-injection delirium/sedation syndrome. Adverse events with signs and symptoms consistent with olanzapine overdose, in particular sedation (including coma) and/or delirium, have been reported following injections. Patients must be observed for at least 3 hours in a certified healthcare setting with ready access to emergency response services, and the product is available only through the ZYPREXA RELPREVV REMS restricted distribution programme requiring prescriber, healthcare setting, patient and pharmacy enrolment (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, Boxed Warning and section 5.2)

CLASS WARNING: cerebrovascular adverse reactions including stroke and transient ischaemic attack, including fatalities, were reported in placebo-controlled trials in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with risperidone, aripiprazole and olanzapine; no studies have been conducted with oral paliperidone, INVEGA SUSTENNA or the 3-month paliperidone palmitate product in elderly patients with dementia (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 5.2; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.2)

CLASS WARNING: tardive dyskinesia, a potentially irreversible syndrome of involuntary dyskinetic movements, with risk increasing with duration of treatment and cumulative dose, and which may develop after relatively brief treatment at low doses (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.5)

CLASS WARNING: neuroleptic malignant syndrome - a potentially fatal symptom complex of hyperpyrexia, muscle rigidity, altered mental status and autonomic instability; management requires immediate discontinuation of antipsychotic drugs, intensive symptomatic treatment and medical monitoring (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS)

CLASS WARNING: QTc prolongation and Torsades de Pointes with haloperidol, with a QTc exceeding 500 msec associated with increased risk; higher-than-recommended doses and intravenous haloperidol appear to confer higher risk (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS)

CLASS WARNING: falls - motor instability, somnolence and orthostatic hypotension reported with antipsychotics may lead to falls and consequent fractures or other fall-related injuries; assess fall risk at initiation and recurrently during treatment (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.8)

CLASS WARNING: leukopenia, neutropenia and agranulocytosis reported temporally related to antipsychotic agents; patients with a history of clinically significant low WBC or drug-induced neutropenia should have CBC monitored frequently during the first few months, and severe neutropenia (absolute neutrophil count < 1000/mm3) requires discontinuation and follow-up of the WBC until recovery (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.9)

CLASS WARNING: hyperprolactinemia from D2 antagonism, with galactorrhoea, amenorrhoea, gynaecomastia and impotence, and reduced bone density with long-standing hyperprolactinemia associated with hypogonadism (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.10; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 5.6)

CLASS WARNING: metabolic changes - hyperglycaemia and diabetes mellitus, sometimes extreme and associated with ketoacidosis, hyperosmolar coma or death, dyslipidaemia and weight gain, reported with all atypical antipsychotics (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.6)
precautions: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: oral tolerability must be established before starting a depot antipsychotic, and patients must be stabilised on antipsychotic medication before conversion to a depot (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 2.3; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 2.2; ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 2.1; UZEDY label, section 2.1)

CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: the depot interval cannot be shortened safely. Because depot release continues for weeks to months, the clinical effects of a dose adjustment may not be apparent for some time - no more often than every 4 weeks for RISPERDAL CONSTA, and possibly several months for INVEGA HAFYERA and INVEGA TRINZA (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 2.3; INVEGA HAFYERA label, section 2.2; INVEGA TRINZA label, section 2.2)

HALOPERIDOL DECANOATE: must not be administered intravenously; give by deep intramuscular injection with a 21 gauge needle, not exceeding 3 mL per injection site (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS and DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION)

HALOPERIDOL DECANOATE: use with caution in patients with severe cardiovascular disorders, with anticonvulsant medications or a history of seizures, with known allergies, and with anticoagulants; haloperidol may impair the antiparkinson effects of levodopa and other dopamine agonists, and if concomitant antiparkinson medication is required it may have to be continued after haloperidol decanoate is discontinued because of the prolonged action; simultaneous discontinuation of both may produce extrapyramidal symptoms (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS)

HALOPERIDOL DECANOATE: if hypotension occurs and a vasopressor is required, epinephrine must not be used because haloperidol may block its vasopressor activity and paradoxical further lowering of blood pressure may occur - use metaraminol, phenylephrine or norepinephrine instead (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS and OVERDOSAGE)

HALOPERIDOL DECANOATE: studies in patients with hepatic impairment have not been conducted; haloperidol concentrations may increase because it is primarily metabolised by the liver and protein binding may decrease (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, Use in Hepatic Impairment)

FLUPHENAZINE DECANOATE: use cautiously in patients who have developed cholestatic jaundice, dermatoses or other allergic reactions to phenothiazine derivatives; in patients exposed to extreme heat or phosphorus insecticides; in patients with a history of convulsive disorders; and in patients with mitral insufficiency, other cardiovascular disease or pheochromocytoma; the physician should be alert to possible 'silent pneumonias' (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS)

FLUPHENAZINE DECANOATE: may cause somnolence, postural hypotension and motor and sensory instability leading to falls; complete fall risk assessments are recommended at initiation and recurrently for long-term therapy (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS)

INVEGA SUSTENNA: not recommended in patients with moderate or severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance < 50 mL/min); in mild renal impairment (50 to < 80 mL/min) initiate with 156 mg on day 1 and 117 mg on day 8, then 78 mg monthly, with a maximum monthly dose of 156 mg (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, sections 2.5 and 8.6). INVEGA HAFYERA is likewise not recommended in moderate or severe renal impairment (INVEGA HAFYERA label, section 2.4)

INVEGA SUSTENNA and INVEGA HAFYERA: use with caution in patients with known cardiovascular disease, cerebrovascular disease or conditions predisposing to hypotension; consider monitoring orthostatic vital signs (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.7)
INVEGA HAFYERA: administer only as a gluteal intramuscular injection once every 6 months by a healthcare professional; do not administer by any other route (INVEGA HAFYERA label, section 2.1)

INVEGA TRINZA: shake the syringe vigorously for at least 15 seconds and inject within 5 minutes; use only the thin wall needles provided; do not re-inject an incompletely administered dose and do not give another dose - monitor and treat with oral supplementation as clinically appropriate until the next scheduled 3-month injection (INVEGA TRINZA label, section 2.1)

ZYPREXA RELPREVV: for deep intramuscular gluteal injection only, not intravenously or subcutaneously; do not confuse with the short-acting ZYPREXA IntraMuscular (10 mg/vial); use a 19-gauge 1.5-inch needle (2-inch for obese patients); aspirate for several seconds and discard the syringe if blood is aspirated; do not massage the injection site (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 2.1)

ZYPREXA RELPREVV: reconstitute only with the diluent supplied in the convenience kit; wear gloves as the powder may irritate the skin; reconstituted product remains stable at room temperature for up to 24 hours in the vial (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 2.2)

RISPERDAL CONSTA: in patients with renal or hepatic impairment, carefully titrate with oral risperidone prior to initiating treatment; do not combine two different dose strengths of RISPERDAL CONSTA in a single administration (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, sections 2.3 and 8.6)
UZEDY: must be administered by a healthcare professional as an abdominal or upper arm subcutaneous injection; do not administer by any other route (UZEDY label, section 2.1)

CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: patients treated with antipsychotics should be reassessed periodically and chronic treatment reserved for those with a chronic illness known to respond to antipsychotic drugs, using the smallest dose and shortest duration producing a satisfactory response (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.5)
serious_adverse_reactions: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (boxed warning on all products in this entry) (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, Boxed Warning; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, Boxed Warning; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, Boxed Warning; ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, Boxed Warning)
Post-injection delirium/sedation syndrome with sedation including coma and/or delirium after olanzapine pamoate injections (boxed warning) (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, Boxed Warning and section 5.1)

Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 5.3; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.3)
Tardive dyskinesia (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.5)

Cerebrovascular adverse reactions including stroke and transient ischaemic attack, with fatalities, in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 5.2; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.2)

Extrapyramidal reactions including parkinsonism, akinesia, akathisia, dystonia, oculogyric crisis, tremor and hyperreflexia, more frequent with the depot phenothiazine fluphenazine decanoate than with haloperidol decanoate (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, ADVERSE REACTIONS Table 1; Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, ADVERSE REACTIONS)
QTc prolongation, ventricular tachycardia, Torsades de Pointes and sudden death with haloperidol (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS and ADVERSE REACTIONS)
Hyperglycaemia and diabetes mellitus, in some cases extreme and associated with ketoacidosis, hyperosmolar coma or death (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.6)
Orthostatic hypotension and syncope with alpha-adrenergic blocking antipsychotics (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.7; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 5.7)
Leukopenia, neutropenia and agranulocytosis (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.9; ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 17)

Seizures: 0.3% (5/1499) of RISPERDAL CONSTA patients in premarketing testing; less than 1% (1/1293) of INVEGA SUSTENNA subjects in the recommended dose range (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 5.11; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.12)

Aspiration pneumonia and dysphagia, with aspiration pneumonia a common cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with advanced Alzheimer's dementia (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 5.12; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.13)
Priapism (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 5.14; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 5.13)

Hepatic injury with cholestatic jaundice, particularly during the first months of phenothiazine therapy, and blood dyscrasias including leukopenia, agranulocytosis, thrombocytopenic and non-thrombocytopenic purpura, eosinophilia and pancytopenia with fluphenazine decanoate (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS)
Encephalopathic syndrome followed by irreversible brain damage with combined lithium and haloperidol therapy (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS)
fields.pregnancy_guidance: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY. Haloperidol decanoate: there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. In rats and rabbits given oral haloperidol at doses 0.5 to 7.5 mg/kg (approximately 0.2 to 7 times the maximum recommended human dose of 20 mg/day on a mg/m2 basis) there was increased resorption, reduced fertility, delayed delivery and pup mortality, with no fetal abnormalities; cleft palate has been observed in mice at 0.5 mg/kg. There are reports of limb malformations following maternal use of haloperidol with other drugs having suspected teratogenic potential in the first trimester, but causal relationships were not established, and haloperidol decanoate should be used during pregnancy only if the benefit clearly justifies a potential risk to the fetus (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, USAGE IN PREGNANCY). Fluphenazine decanoate: neonates exposed to antipsychotic drugs during the third trimester of pregnancy are at risk for extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms following delivery, with reports of agitation, hypertonia, hypotonia, tremor, somnolence, respiratory distress and feeding disorder; fluphenazine decanoate should be used during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS - Pregnancy Non-teratogenic Effects). Risperidone and paliperidone depots: neonates exposed to antipsychotic drugs during the third trimester of pregnancy are at risk for extrapyramidal and/or withdrawal symptoms following delivery. Overall, available data from published epidemiologic studies of pregnant women exposed to risperidone or to paliperidone have not established a drug-associated risk for major birth defects, miscarriage, or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes, and there are risks to the mother associated with untreated schizophrenia or bipolar I disorder and with exposure to antipsychotics during pregnancy. Risperidone has been detected in plasma in adult subjects up to 8 weeks after a single-dose administration of RISPERDAL CONSTA, and paliperidone has been detected in plasma in adult subjects up to 126 days after a single-dose administration of INVEGA SUSTENNA; the clinical significance of administration before pregnancy or during pregnancy is not known (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 8.1; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 8.1).
fields.lactation_guidance: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY. Haloperidol decanoate: since haloperidol is excreted in human breast milk, infants should not be nursed during treatment with haloperidol decanoate (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, NURSING MOTHERS). Risperidone: limited data from published literature report the presence of risperidone and its metabolite 9-hydroxyrisperidone in human breast milk at a relative infant dose of 2.3% to 4.7% of the maternal weight-adjusted dosage, with reports of sedation, failure to thrive, jitteriness and extrapyramidal symptoms in breastfed infants exposed to risperidone; risperidone has been detected in plasma up to 8 weeks after a single dose of RISPERDAL CONSTA and the clinical significance for the breastfed infant is not known (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 8.2). Paliperidone: limited data from published literature report the presence of paliperidone in human breast milk, with reports of sedation, failure to thrive, jitteriness and extrapyramidal symptoms in breastfed infants exposed to risperidone; paliperidone has been detected in plasma up to 126 days after a single dose of INVEGA SUSTENNA and the clinical significance for the breastfed infant is not known (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 8.2). In both cases the developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered along with the mother's clinical need for the depot antipsychotic and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child, and breastfed infants should be monitored for excess sedation, failure to thrive, jitteriness and extrapyramidal symptoms.
fields.overdose: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: the depot products have no specific antidote and overdose is harder to reverse because of the prolonged release. Haloperidol decanoate: symptoms of overdosage would be an exaggeration of known pharmacologic effects, most prominently severe extrapyramidal reactions, hypotension or sedation, with the patient appearing comatose with respiratory depression and hypotension severe enough to produce a shock-like state; because there is no specific antidote, treatment is primarily supportive, dialysis is not recommended because it removes only very small amounts of haloperidol, epinephrine must not be used, and antiparkinson medication should be administered for severe extrapyramidal reactions and continued for several weeks then withdrawn gradually. ECG and vital signs should be monitored for QTc prolongation or dysrhythmias until the ECG is normal (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, OVERDOSAGE). ZYPREXA RELPREVV: there is no specific antidote to olanzapine, so appropriate supportive measures should be initiated; hypotension and circulatory collapse should be treated with intravenous fluids and/or sympathomimetic agents, but epinephrine, dopamine or other sympathomimetics with beta-agonist activity must not be used because beta stimulation may worsen hypotension in the setting of olanzapine-induced alpha blockade; respiratory support including ventilation may be required, and cardiovascular monitoring including continuous ECG should commence immediately (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 10.2).
fields.pharmacokinetics: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: depot kinetics differ by product and determine the dosing interval. Haloperidol decanoate: administration in sesame oil results in slow and sustained release of haloperidol, with plasma concentrations gradually rising to a peak at about 6 days after injection and falling thereafter, with an apparent half-life of about 3 weeks; steady-state plasma concentrations are achieved within 2 to 4 months in patients receiving monthly injections, and the relationship between dose and plasma concentration is roughly linear below 450 mg, though pharmacokinetics can be quite variable between subjects (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY). RISPERDAL CONSTA: after a single gluteal IM injection there is a small initial release of the drug (less than 1% of the dose) followed by a lag time of 3 weeks; the main release starts from 3 weeks onward, is maintained from 4 to 6 weeks and subsides by 7 weeks; steady-state plasma concentrations are reached after 4 injections and maintained for 4 to 6 weeks after the last injection; deltoid and gluteal injections are bioequivalent; pharmacokinetics are linear over 12.5 to 50 mg (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 12.3). INVEGA SUSTENNA: following IM injection, plasma concentrations of paliperidone gradually rise to a median Tmax of 13 days, with release starting as early as day 1 and lasting as long as 126 days; the median apparent half-life of paliperidone following single-dose administration over the 39 to 234 mg range was 25 to 49 days; the apparent volume of distribution is 391 L and plasma protein binding is 74% (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 12.3). INVEGA TRINZA and INVEGA HAFYERA extend this profile to three-monthly and six-monthly intervals (INVEGA TRINZA label, section 2.2; INVEGA HAFYERA label, section 2.2). ZYPREXA RELPREVV: slow dissolution of the practically insoluble olanzapine salt after deep IM gluteal injection results in prolonged systemic olanzapine plasma concentrations sustained over weeks to months, with an effective half-life of approximately 30 days compared with approximately 30 hours after oral administration, and exposure may persist for months after an injection; a 300 mg dose every two weeks delivers approximately 20 mg olanzapine per day and 150 mg every two weeks delivers approximately 10 mg per day (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 12.3).
clinical_pearls: This entry is a CLASS entry and not a single drug: dosing, route, interval, monitoring and contraindications differ between haloperidol decanoate, fluphenazine decanoate, RISPERDAL CONSTA, UZEDY, INVEGA SUSTENNA, INVEGA TRINZA, INVEGA HAFYERA and ZYPREXA RELPREVV, and one product's regimen must never be substituted for another's.

The universal rule for every depot antipsychotic is to establish oral tolerability first and to stabilise the patient before conversion, because a depot dose cannot be quickly withdrawn or reversed (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 2.3; ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 2.1).

The longer the interval, the slower the feedback loop: with INVEGA HAFYERA and INVEGA TRINZA a dose adjustment may take months to show, and with RISPERDAL CONSTA upward adjustment should be no more frequent than every 4 weeks (INVEGA HAFYERA label, section 2.2; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, section 2.3).

Do not use unfractionated heparin after a dose of a depot - that is specific to andexanet alfa, not to antipsychotics; the relevant depot warning is that epinephrine must not be used for hypotension with haloperidol because it can paradoxically lower blood pressure further (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, PRECAUTIONS).

Every depot antipsychotic carries the dementia-related psychosis mortality boxed warning, and none of them is approved for dementia-related psychosis (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, Boxed Warning; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, Boxed Warning; ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, Boxed Warning).

Olanzapine pamoate is the only depot in this class with a second boxed warning: post-injection delirium/sedation syndrome, which occurs in about 2% of patients over up to 46 months and mandates a certified healthcare setting, 3 hours of continuous observation after every injection, and REMS enrolment (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, Boxed Warning, sections 5.1 and 5.2).

The escalation pathway for the depot formulations is product-specific but conceptually fixed: oral -> monthly depot -> three-monthly (INVEGA TRINZA) -> six-monthly (INVEGA HAFYERA), and each step requires a defined period of toleration on the previous step (INVEGA TRINZA label, section 1; INVEGA HAFYERA label, section 1).

For total drug burden, remember the depot half-lives: haloperidol decanoate about 3 weeks, paliperidone after INVEGA SUSTENNA 25 to 49 days, olanzapine after ZYPREXA RELPREVV about 30 days effective (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, CLINICAL PHARMACOLOGY; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 12.3; ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, section 12.3).

For LMIC procurement, the WHO Model List of Essential Medicines (24th list, 2025) lists fluphenazine 25 mg/mL decanoate/enanthate for intramuscular use and haloperidol decanoate as a therapeutic equivalent, and the Kenya Essential Medicines List 2023 lists fluphenazine oily depot injection 25 mg/mL and haloperidol oily injection 50 mg/1 mL, both at Level of Use 4 (primary hospital); the second-generation depots are not on either list.

Adjunctive safety review before every depot refill: ECG/QTc and electrolytes, prolactin, fasting glucose and weight, orthostatic vitals and fall risk, CBC, and an extrapyramidal plus tardive dyskinesia examination (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, WARNINGS and PRECAUTIONS; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, sections 5.4, 5.6, 5.7, 5.9 and 5.10).
black_box_warnings: CLASS WARNING (present on every depot antipsychotic in this entry): INCREASED MORTALITY IN ELDERLY PATIENTS WITH DEMENTIA-RELATED PSYCHOSIS. Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis treated with antipsychotic drugs are at an increased risk of death. Analyses of seventeen placebo-controlled trials (modal duration of 10 weeks), largely in patients taking atypical antipsychotic drugs, revealed a risk of death in drug-treated patients of between 1.6 to 1.7 times the risk of death in placebo-treated patients; over the course of a typical 10-week controlled trial the rate of death in drug-treated patients was about 4.5% compared with about 2.6% in the placebo group, with most deaths appearing cardiovascular or infectious in nature. Observational studies suggest that, similar to atypical antipsychotic drugs, treatment with conventional antipsychotic drugs may increase mortality. None of the depot products covered by this entry is approved for the treatment of patients with dementia-related psychosis (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, Boxed Warning; Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, Boxed Warning; RISPERDAL CONSTA label, Boxed Warning; UZEDY label, Boxed Warning; INVEGA SUSTENNA label, Boxed Warning; INVEGA TRINZA label, Boxed Warning; INVEGA HAFYERA label, Boxed Warning; ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, Boxed Warning).

PRODUCT-SPECIFIC BOXED WARNING (olanzapine pamoate / ZYPREXA RELPREVV only): POST-INJECTION DELIRIUM/SEDATION SYNDROME. Adverse events with signs and symptoms consistent with olanzapine overdose, in particular sedation (including coma) and/or delirium, have been reported following injections of ZYPREXA RELPREVV. ZYPREXA RELPREVV must be administered in a certified healthcare setting with ready access to emergency response services, and after each injection patients must be observed at the healthcare setting by a healthcare professional for at least 3 hours. Because of this risk, ZYPREXA RELPREVV is available only through the restricted distribution ZYPREXA RELPREVV REMS programme, which requires prescriber, healthcare setting, patient and pharmacy enrolment (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, Boxed Warning).
fields.renal_dose_adjustment: PRODUCT-SPECIFIC. INVEGA SUSTENNA is not recommended in patients with moderate or severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance < 50 mL/min); in mild renal impairment (creatinine clearance 50 to < 80 mL/min) initiate with 156 mg on day 1 and 117 mg on day 8, then 78 mg monthly, with a maximum monthly dose of 156 mg, adjusting within the 39, 78, 117 and 156 mg strengths (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, sections 2.5 and 8.6). INVEGA HAFYERA is not recommended in patients with moderate or severe renal impairment; in mild renal impairment the patient should be adjusted and stabilised with a once-a-month product before transitioning (INVEGA HAFYERA label, section 2.4). RISPERDAL CONSTA: patients with renal impairment may have less ability to eliminate risperidone, so carefully titrate with oral risperidone before initiating, and dose reduction as low as 12.5 mg may be appropriate (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, sections 2.3, 2.4 and 8.6). INVEGA TRINZA and UZEDY: no renal impairment adjustment is specified in the label sections for INVEGA TRINZA, while UZEDY requires establishing tolerability with oral risperidone before initiation (UZEDY label, section 2.1). Haloperidol decanoate and fluphenazine decanoate labels specify no renal dose adjustment (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION; Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION).
fields.hepatic_dose_adjustment: PRODUCT-SPECIFIC. INVEGA SUSTENNA has not been studied in patients with hepatic impairment; based on a study with oral paliperidone no dose adjustment is required in patients with mild or moderate hepatic impairment, and paliperidone has not been studied in severe hepatic impairment (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 8.7). RISPERDAL CONSTA: patients with impaired hepatic function may have an increase in the free fraction of risperidone, possibly resulting in an enhanced effect, so carefully titrate with oral risperidone before initiating, and dose reduction as low as 12.5 mg may be appropriate (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, sections 2.3, 2.4 and 8.6). Haloperidol decanoate: studies in patients with hepatic impairment have not been conducted, and haloperidol concentrations may increase in hepatically impaired patients because it is primarily metabolised by the liver and protein binding may decrease (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, Use in Hepatic Impairment). Fluphenazine decanoate: the presence of blood dyscrasia or liver damage precludes use, and liver damage as cholestatic jaundice may be encountered particularly during the first months of therapy, with treatment to be discontinued if this occurs (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, CONTRAINDICATIONS and PRECAUTIONS).
fields.administration_instructions: CLASS-LEVEL ENTRY: all injections in this class must be administered by a healthcare professional and are not for intravenous use unless a specific product states otherwise. Haloperidol decanoate: deep intramuscular injection, 21 gauge needle recommended, maximum 3 mL per injection site, DO NOT ADMINISTER INTRAVENOUSLY; visually inspect for particulate matter and discoloration before administration (Haloperidol Decanoate Injection label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION). Fluphenazine decanoate: may be given intramuscularly or subcutaneously; use a dry syringe and needle of at least 21 gauge, as a wet needle or syringe may cause the solution to become cloudy; visually inspect before administration (Fluphenazine Decanoate Injection label, DOSAGE AND ADMINISTRATION). RISPERDAL CONSTA: intramuscular injection into the deltoid or gluteal muscle using the supplied needles, with deltoid and gluteal sites interchangeable; give oral risperidone with the first injection and continue for 3 weeks (RISPERDAL CONSTA label, sections 2.3 and 12.3). UZEDY: abdominal or upper arm subcutaneous injection by a healthcare professional; do not administer by any other route (UZEDY label, section 2.1). INVEGA SUSTENNA: intramuscular use only, single injection, injected slowly deep into the deltoid or gluteal muscle using only the provided needles, alternating deltoid injections between the two deltoid muscles and gluteal injections into the upper-outer quadrant of the gluteal muscle (INVEGA SUSTENNA label, section 2.1). INVEGA TRINZA: intramuscular only, shake the syringe vigorously for at least 15 seconds and inject within 5 minutes using only the provided thin wall needles (INVEGA TRINZA label, section 2.1). INVEGA HAFYERA: gluteal intramuscular injection once every 6 months by a healthcare professional; do not administer by any other route (INVEGA HAFYERA label, section 2.1). ZYPREXA RELPREVV: deep intramuscular gluteal injection only, not intravenously or subcutaneously, using a 19-gauge 1.5-inch needle, aspirating for several seconds and discarding the syringe if blood is aspirated, not massaging the injection site; must be given in a certified healthcare setting with 3 hours of observation and REMS enrolment (ZYPREXA RELPREVV label, sections 2.1, 2.2 and 5.2).

The draft covers eight representative depot products, each sourced to its own current FDA label: haloperidol decanoate, fluphenazine decanoate, RISPERDAL CONSTA (risperidone LAR, IM), UZEDY (risperidone extended release, SC), INVEGA SUSTENNA (paliperidone palmitate monthly), INVEGA TRINZA (3-monthly), INVEGA HAFYERA (6-monthly) and ZYPREXA RELPREVV (olanzapine pamoate). The previous row content (olanzapine label text, including the antipsychotic dementia boxed warning) has been replaced by this properly sourced class draft, and the dementia-related psychosis mortality boxed warning that had been wrongly attributed to an unrelated drug is retained here because it genuinely applies to every product in this class. ZYPREXA RELPREVV is the only product in this entry with an additional boxed warning (post-injection delirium/sedation syndrome) and with a REMS requirement and mandatory 3-hour post-injection observation. For WHO Model List and Kenya list context, the only depot antipsychotics on the WHO eEML (24th list, 2025) are fluphenazine decanoate/enanthate IM and haloperidol decanoate (an equivalent of fluphenazine), and the KEML 2023 lists fluphenazine oily depot injection 25 mg/mL and haloperidol oily injection 50 mg/1 mL, both at Level of Use 4 (primary hospital); none of the second-generation depots is on either list, which is why those products are included on the strength of their FDA labels rather than list status. There is no product in this class with a paediatric indication.
